skills.observableOutcome: Identifies the value of a digit in a three-digit number.
Solves an addition problem with two two-digit addends.
Identifies a suitable habitat for an animal and connects living things to their environments.
Selects a familiar English word that completes a simple context sentence.
Recognizes a correctly ordered simple English sentence.
Identifies plants as living things using observable evidence such as growth and change.
Names common plant parts and connects selected parts with their functions and edible uses.
Traces familiar foods and useful materials to plant sources.
Describes early seed germination and identifies conditions that support seedling growth.
Compares plants fairly using observable features and consistent measurements.
Records visible changes during a simple supervised observation.
Observes plants safely and avoids tasting or damaging unknown plants.

activities.prompt: In 472, what is the value of the digit 7?
في العدد ٤٧٢، ما قيمة الرقم ٧؟
activities.feedbackCorrect: صحيح! الرقم ٧ في منزلة العشرات، فقيمته ٧٠.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: انظر إلى منزلة الرقم ٧ في العدد.

activities.prompt: A basket has 26 oranges. Add 13 more. How many oranges are there now?
في سلة ٢٦ برتقالة، أضفنا إليها ١٣ برتقالة. كم برتقالة أصبحت في السلة؟
A pencil is 14 cm long. A ruler is 20 cm long. Which is longer?
طول قلم ١٤ سم، وطول مسطرة ٢٠ سم. أيهما أطول؟
Which place is a suitable habitat for a fish?
أي مكان يُعد موطناً مناسباً للسمكة؟
activities.feedbackCorrect: صحيح! يوفر النهر الماء الذي تحتاجه السمكة.

activities.prompt: Choose the word to complete the sentence: The camel lives in the ____.
اختر الكلمة الإنجليزية الصحيحة لإكمال الجملة: The camel lives in the ____.
activities.feedbackCorrect: أحسنت! كلمة desert تكمل الجملة بشكل صحيح.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: اختر كلمة تدل على مكان يمكن أن يعيش فيه الجمل.

activities.prompt: Choose the correctly ordered English sentence.
اختر الجملة الإنجليزية الصحيحة في ترتيب الكلمات.
activities.feedbackCorrect: صحيح! ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الأولى سليم.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: اقرأ كل جملة بالإنجليزية وتحقق من ترتيب كلماتها.

activities.prompt: In 361, what is the value of the digit 6?
There are 34 red beads and 25 blue beads. How many beads are there altogether?
A desk is 120 cm long. A table is 95 cm long. Which is longer?
Which place is a suitable habitat for a camel?
The sky is dark and the clouds are thick. It may ____.
Which sentence has the words in the correct order?
Which one is a living plant?

optionRationales.a: Came from a plant but is no longer living
optionRationales.b: Living and growing

activities.prompt: Which observation is evidence that a plant is living?

options.text: It moves when the wind blows

optionRationales.b: Paint is not growth
optionRationales.c: New growth is evidence of life

activities.prompt: What do many green plants use light for?

options.text: Holding the plant in the soil

optionRationales.a: Light supplies energy for making food
optionRationales.b: Roots mainly take in water

activities.prompt: Two plants are in pots. Which is the fairest way to compare their growth?

options.text: Choose the pot that looks nicer
Measure their heights in the same way

optionRationales.b: The same measure provides comparable evidence

activities.prompt: Which condition is important for the healthy growth of most green plants?

options.text: A plastic cover around every leaf

optionRationales.a: A plastic cover is not a general plant need
optionRationales.b: Music is not a required growth condition

activities.prompt: A plant stays in one place, but its stem becomes longer. What does this show?

options.text: It cannot be living because it does not walk
It is changing only because the pot is larger

optionRationales.a: Growth is a sign of life
optionRationales.b: Plants do not need to walk
optionRationales.c: Pot size alone does not explain stem growth

activities.prompt: Which statement about plants is accurate?

options.text: All plants have the same size and shape
Plants can differ in size, shape and leaf form
Only plants with flowers are living

optionRationales.b: Plants have many forms
optionRationales.c: Many living plants are not flowering when observed

activities.prompt: How should you observe a plant outdoors?

options.text: Pull it from the ground to inspect it
Taste a leaf to identify it
Look carefully and avoid damaging it

optionRationales.b: Unknown plants may be unsafe to taste

activities.prompt: Which plant part usually takes in water from the soil?

optionRationales.b: Fruits often contain seeds

activities.prompt: Which part supports many plant leaves and flowers?

optionRationales.a: The stem supports the plant and transports materials
optionRationales.b: A seed can grow into a plant
optionRationales.c: A fruit protects seeds in many plants

activities.prompt: Which plant part helps many green plants make food using light?

optionRationales.b: Leaves are major photosynthetic organs

activities.prompt: Which part of a carrot do people usually eat?

optionRationales.b: A carrot is not a botanical fruit
optionRationales.c: The edible carrot part is a storage root

activities.prompt: Which food is an example of seeds that people eat?

optionRationales.b: Lettuce leaves are leaves

activities.prompt: Which part of the broccoli plant do we commonly eat?

optionRationales.b: Broccoli is commonly eaten as immature flower structures

activities.prompt: Which statement about a potato is correct?

options.text: It is the root of the plant
It is the fruit of the plant
It is a modified underground stem (tuber)

optionRationales.b: A potato is not a botanical fruit
optionRationales.c: A potato tuber is a modified underground stem

activities.prompt: You find an unfamiliar wild plant. You do not know whether it is safe to eat. What should you do?

options.text: Do not eat it; ask a trusted adult
Feed it to a pet to test it

optionRationales.b: Tasting unknown plants is unsafe

activities.prompt: Cotton fibres used to make some clothes come from which source?

optionRationales.a: Sheep wool is an animal fibre, not cotton
optionRationales.b: Cotton is a plant source

activities.prompt: Which plant material is commonly used to make paper?

optionRationales.b: Sand is not the usual paper fibre
optionRationales.c: Wood fibres are a common plant-based source

activities.prompt: Sesame oil is made from which part of a plant?

optionRationales.a: Sesame oil is pressed from seeds
optionRationales.b: Roots are not the usual source
optionRationales.c: Flowers are not the usual source

activities.prompt: A family grows a date palm. Which pair describes two useful things it can provide?

optionRationales.a: These are not produced by the palm
optionRationales.b: Date palms provide dates and shade
optionRationales.c: These are not direct palm products

activities.prompt: Which food is made from a plant grain?

optionRationales.b: Eggs are animal products
optionRationales.c: Sorghum flour is milled from a grain

activities.prompt: Which pair includes two products that can come from plants?

optionRationales.b: Glass and iron are not plant materials
optionRationales.c: Fish and eggs are animal products

activities.prompt: Paper has been made from wood and changed in a factory. What is its original source?

options.text: It has become an animal product
It still has a plant source
It came from the soil as ready-made paper

optionRationales.a: Processing does not change its source category
optionRationales.b: Paper made from wood still has a plant source

activities.prompt: Which action shows care for useful plants?

options.text: Pull up seedlings to see their roots
Water plants appropriately and avoid damaging them

optionRationales.b: This harms seedlings

activities.prompt: What does germination mean?

optionRationales.b: Leaf fall is unrelated
optionRationales.c: Germination is when a seed begins to grow

activities.prompt: Which part commonly appears first when a bean seed starts to germinate?

optionRationales.b: A flower develops later

activities.prompt: Which conditions help many common seeds begin to germinate?

options.text: Bright light, soil and fertiliser only
A sealed container filled with water

optionRationales.a: Light and soil are not universal requirements for germination
optionRationales.b: Water, air and suitable warmth support germination

activities.prompt: A seedling has green leaves. What helps the green plant make food?

optionRationales.a: Sound is not a food-making requirement
optionRationales.b: Soil colour does not provide energy

activities.prompt: You are watching beans germinate on damp paper with an adult. What is the best way to record what happens?

options.text: Draw or note visible changes each day
Open the container and taste a seed

optionRationales.b: Tasting experimental seeds is unsafe and unnecessary

activities.prompt: Which order shows a simple early stage of bean growth?

optionRationales.a: This is not the early germination sequence
optionRationales.b: This is a plausible early growth sequence
optionRationales.c: These items do not form a growth sequence

activities.prompt: Why should the paper around a germinating seed be damp, not flooded?

options.text: Seeds need to float all the time
More water always makes seeds grow faster

optionRationales.b: Excess water can reduce available air

activities.prompt: A bean begins to germinate on damp paper before it is planted in soil. What does this show?

options.text: Soil is not always needed for germination to begin
Seeds never need soil as plants grow

optionRationales.b: Soil supports later plant growth and many plant needs

lessons.title: Parts of Plants and Plants We Eat
